content:
Node Postprocessor Modules
SimilarityPostprocessor
Section titled “SimilarityPostprocessor”Used to remove nodes that are below a similarity score threshold.
KeywordNodePostprocessor
Section titled “KeywordNodePostprocessor”Used to ensure certain keywords are either excluded or included.
MetadataReplacementPostProcessor
Section titled “MetadataReplacementPostProcessor”Used to replace the node content with a field from the node metadata. If the field is not present in the metadata, then the node text remains unchanged. Most useful when used in combination with the SentenceWindowNodeParser.
LongContextReorder
Section titled “LongContextReorder”Models struggle to access significant details found in the center of extended contexts. A study observed that the best performance typically arises when crucial data is positioned at the start or conclusion of the input context. Additionally, as the input context lengthens, performance drops notably, even in models designed for long contexts.
This module will re-order the retrieved nodes, which can be helpful in cases where a large top-k is needed.
SentenceEmbeddingOptimizer
Section titled “SentenceEmbeddingOptimizer”This postprocessor optimizes token usage by removing sentences that are not relevant to the query (this is done using embeddings).
The percentile cutoff is a measure for using the top percentage of relevant sentences.
The threshold cutoff can be specified instead, which uses a raw similarity cutoff for picking which sentences to keep.
A full notebook guide can be found here
CohereRerank
Section titled “CohereRerank”Uses the “Cohere ReRank” functionality to re-order nodes, and returns the top N nodes.
Full notebook guide is available here.
SentenceTransformerRerank
Section titled “SentenceTransformerRerank”Uses the cross-encoders from the sentence-transformer package to re-order nodes, and returns the top N nodes.
Full notebook guide is available here.
Please also refer to the sentence-transformer docs for a more complete list of models (and also shows tradeoffs in speed/accuracy). The default model is cross-encoder/ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2, which provides the most speed.
LLM Rerank
Section titled “LLM Rerank”Uses a LLM to re-order nodes by asking the LLM to return the relevant documents and a score of how relevant they are. Returns the top N ranked nodes.
Full notebook guide is available her for Gatsby and here for Lyft 10K documents.
JinaRerank
Section titled “JinaRerank”Uses the “Jina ReRank” functionality to re-order nodes, and returns the top N nodes.
Full notebook guide is available here.
FixedRecencyPostprocessor
Section titled “FixedRecencyPostprocessor”This postprocessor returns the top K nodes sorted by date. This assumes there is a date field to parse in the metadata of each node.
A full notebook guide is available here.
EmbeddingRecencyPostprocessor
Section titled “EmbeddingRecencyPostprocessor”This postprocessor returns the top K nodes after sorting by date and removing older nodes that are too similar after measuring embedding similarity.
A full notebook guide is available here.
TimeWeightedPostprocessor
Section titled “TimeWeightedPostprocessor”This postprocessor returns the top K nodes applying a time-weighted rerank to each node. Each time a node is retrieved, the time it was retrieved is recorded. This biases search to favor information that has not been returned in a query yet.
A full notebook guide is available here.
(Beta) PIINodePostprocessor
Section titled “(Beta) PIINodePostprocessor”The PII (Personal Identifiable Information) postprocessor removes information that might be a security risk. It does this by using NER (either with a dedicated NER model, or with a local LLM model).
LLM Version
Section titled “LLM Version”NER Version
Section titled “NER Version”This version uses the default local model from Hugging Face that is loaded when you run pipeline("ner").
A full notebook guide for both can be found here.
(Beta) PrevNextNodePostprocessor
Section titled “(Beta) PrevNextNodePostprocessor”Uses pre-defined settings to read the Node relationships and fetch either all nodes that come previously, next, or both.
This is useful when you know the relationships point to important data (either before, after, or both) that should be sent to the LLM if that node is retrieved.
(Beta) AutoPrevNextNodePostprocessor
Section titled “(Beta) AutoPrevNextNodePostprocessor”The same as PrevNextNodePostprocessor, but lets the LLM decide the mode (next, previous, or both).
A full example notebook is available here.
(Beta) RankGPT
Section titled “(Beta) RankGPT”Uses RankGPT agent to rerank documents according to relevance. Returns the top N ranked nodes.
Full notebook guide is available here.
Colbert Reranker
Section titled “Colbert Reranker”Uses Colbert V2 model as a reranker to rerank documents according to the fine-grained similarity between query tokens and passage tokens. Returns the top N ranked nodes.
Full notebook guide is available here.
rankLLM
Section titled “rankLLM”Uses models from rankLLM to rerank documents. Returns the top N ranked nodes.
A full notebook example is available.
